title: Samson's Riddle and Marriage
overview: Judges 14 narrates a pivotal episode in the life of Samson, Israel's Nazirite judge, focusing on his controversial marriage to a Philistine woman and the subsequent riddle he poses to her people. This chapter highlights Samson’s personal desires intertwined with God’s sovereign purpose to challenge Philistine dominance. It reveals the tension between divine providence and human weakness, as Samson’s actions set the stage for conflict with the Philistines. The chapter also introduces themes of temptation, secrecy, and divine empowerment, illustrating how God uses Samson’s life to advance His plan despite Samson’s flawed decisions. This story is significant within Judges as it marks the beginning of Samson’s confrontations with the Philistines, emphasizing God’s ongoing deliverance of Israel through imperfect instruments.
structure:
**Verses 1-4: Samson’s Desire for a Philistine Wife.** The chapter opens with Samson’s decision to marry a Philistine woman, despite parental objections and cultural prohibitions. This section sets the stage for conflict by highlighting Samson’s personal choice and God’s hidden purpose to use this union against the Philistines.

**Verses 5-9: The Lion and the Honey.** On the way to claim his bride, Samson encounters and kills a lion by the Spirit of the LORD. Later, he discovers honey in the lion’s carcass, which becomes the basis for his riddle. This section symbolizes God’s empowerment and foreshadows the coming conflict.

**Verses 10-20: The Wedding Feast and the Riddle.** Samson hosts a feast, poses a riddle to the Philistine guests, and faces deception through his wife. The breach of trust leads to Samson’s violent retaliation, the loss of his wife, and escalating tensions with the Philistines. This section reveals themes of betrayal, cunning, and divine judgment.

keyVerses.text: But his father and his mother knew not that it was of the LORD, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines: for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals God’s sovereign hand behind Samson’s seemingly personal decisions, showing that God uses human actions—even flawed ones—to fulfill His purposes, particularly in opposing Israel’s enemies.

keyVerses.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the divine empowerment of Samson by the Spirit of the LORD, enabling him to perform superhuman feats. It underscores the theme of God’s enabling presence in the life of His chosen judge.

keyVerses.text: And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.
keyVerses.significance: The riddle encapsulates the paradox of life and God’s providence—sweetness emerging from strength and death. It symbolizes God’s ability to bring blessing and victory from seemingly impossible circumstances.

keyVerses.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, and slew thirty men of them, and took their spoil, and gave change of garments unto them which expounded the riddle. And his anger was kindled, and he went up to his father's house.
keyVerses.significance: This verse shows God’s Spirit empowering Samson again for judgment against the Philistines, demonstrating divine justice and the consequences of betrayal and deceit.

characters.name: Samson
characters.description: The Nazirite judge of Israel, known for his supernatural strength given by the Spirit of the LORD. In this chapter, he pursues a Philistine wife, poses a riddle, and enacts violent retribution, illustrating both his flawed human desires and God’s empowerment.

characters.name: Samson’s Wife
characters.description: A Philistine woman from Timnath whom Samson desires and marries. She is used by the Philistines to extract the answer to Samson’s riddle, resulting in betrayal and the loss of her place as Samson’s wife.

characters.name: The Philistines
characters.description: The dominant enemy nation over Israel at this time. They interact with Samson through his marriage and the riddle, ultimately provoking conflict that highlights the ongoing struggle between Israel and the Philistines.

characters.name: The Spirit of the LORD
characters.description: The divine presence empowering Samson to perform extraordinary feats, including killing the lion and slaying thirty Philistines. The Spirit’s coming signifies God’s active role in Samson’s mission.

themes.description: Samson’s personal choices, including marrying a Philistine woman, are used by God to fulfill His sovereign plan against Israel’s enemies, demonstrating how divine providence works through human actions.

themes.theme: Conflict Between Israel and the Philistines
themes.description: The chapter portrays the tension and hostility between Israel and the Philistines, setting the stage for ongoing conflict and God’s deliverance through Samson.
Samson’s feats of strength are enabled by the Spirit of the LORD, emphasizing the necessity of divine power for God’s purposes to be accomplished.
The Philistines’ use of Samson’s wife to solve the riddle introduces themes of betrayal and the consequences of broken trust within relationships.

historicalContext: Judges 14 is set during the period of the Judges, approximately in the late Bronze Age to early Iron Age (circa 1100–1050 BC), a time when Israel lacked centralized leadership and was frequently oppressed by surrounding nations, notably the Philistines. Timnath, the location of Samson’s marriage, was a Philistine-controlled city, reflecting the political dominance of the Philistines over Israel during this era. Marriages between Israelites and Philistines were culturally and religiously contentious, as intermarriage was often forbidden to preserve Israel’s distinct identity and covenant relationship with God. The wedding feast and riddle customs reflect ancient Near Eastern social practices, where riddles and contests were common forms of entertainment and social interaction. The narrative also reflects the ongoing struggle for Israel’s deliverance from foreign domination through God’s chosen judges.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This perspective emphasizes God’s sovereign control over Samson’s life and actions, interpreting his marriage and conflicts as part of God’s providential plan to judge Israel’s enemies and discipline His people.

Dispensationalists see Samson’s story as part of God’s unfolding plan for Israel, highlighting the role of the Spirit’s empowerment in the period before the monarchy and the Messianic kingdom, with Samson as a type of Christ in strength and deliverance.

Early church interpreters often viewed Samson’s life allegorically, seeing his struggles with the Philistines as symbolic of the Christian’s battle against sin and the devil, with the Spirit’s power representing divine grace.

crossReferences.connection: David’s encounter with a lion and bear parallels Samson’s killing of the lion, both demonstrating God’s empowerment of His chosen deliverers.
The imagery of sweetness and strength in Samson’s riddle echoes wisdom literature’s use of metaphor to convey deeper truths.
Jesus’ teaching on abiding in Him to bear fruit parallels the necessity of the Spirit’s empowerment seen in Samson’s feats.
Paul’s teaching on the Spirit giving life to believers connects with the Spirit of the LORD empowering Samson for his mission.
The story of Dinah’s marriage and conflict with the Canaanites provides a background for understanding the dangers of intermarriage with hostile peoples.

application: Trust in God’s sovereign plan even when personal desires seem contrary to His ways.
Seek the empowerment of the Holy Spirit for strength to face life’s challenges and spiritual battles.
Be cautious of relationships that may lead to spiritual compromise or conflict.
Practice wisdom in communication, avoiding secrecy that can lead to betrayal.
Respond to betrayal and injustice with faith in God’s justice rather than personal vengeance.
Recognize that God can bring good from difficult and unexpected circumstances.
conclusion: Judges 14 presents a complex portrait of Samson as a flawed yet divinely empowered judge whose personal choices intersect with God’s sovereign plan to challenge the Philistines. The chapter underscores themes of divine sovereignty, human weakness, and the Spirit’s enabling power, reminding believers that God can use imperfect vessels to accomplish His purposes. It also warns of the dangers of disobedience and misplaced trust, encouraging reliance on God’s guidance and strength. For modern Christians, this chapter calls for faithfulness, wisdom in relationships, and confidence that God’s Spirit empowers His people to overcome adversity.
timeline: c. 1100 BC - Period of the Judges, during Philistine domination over Israel

definitions.definition: In the riddle, 'eater' refers to the lion that consumed prey, symbolizing strength and danger.
A set of clothing given as a prize or reward, indicating honor or payment in ancient customs.
The dead body of an animal, in this case, the lion’s carcass where Samson found honey.
The empowering presence of God enabling Samson to perform supernatural feats.
